newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Cocoa called higher after fund-led slide.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Cocoa called higher after fund-led slide.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Cocoa futures were expected to stage a slight corrective bounce on Friday after a recent wave of fund-led long liquidation, traders and technical analysts said.

London's benchmark September contract tumbled to two-month lows on Thursday -- hitting but not breaking nearby support at the psychological 1,000 stg barrier -- in heavy volume as funds liquidated their long positions.
The slide escalated as New York took a further dive on speculative and fund long liquidation ahead of the long weekend with the July 4 Independence Day holiday.

But traders called London to open around nine stg higher on Thursday, citing a constructive close and currency factors. September closed at 1,019 stg, still sharply down on the day but 19 stg up on the session low.
However, in the absence of the New York market activity in London was expected to be muted, they said.
"It was unable to hold above the peak we had in March and April. It did bounce quite well and came back later in the session," said Susan Rigg, a technical analyst at Chart Analysis.

If September continued to move lower and trade under 1,000 stg, then prices were likely to test lower support levels in a trading band seen in the first quarter of this year, approximately from 895 to 980 stg.
"If it moves back below that area and starts closing down there I think we will then see a further test of support as it comes into the mid-December to March base area," Rigg said.
Fundamental news included the second-quarter Dutch cocoa grind, which rose 10.4 percent to 100,132 tonnes from 90,724 tonnes in the same period of 1996.
Analysts had expected a modest rise.
